entries.test: Contemporaneous surveys and public positions of AI researchers and industry leaders would show whether skepticism that LLM scaling can deliver AGI had become a mainstream view by September 2025.
entries.note: Mainstream need not mean unanimous or the majority view.

entries.test: A publicly demonstrated, independently evaluated AGI produced through LLM scaling would falsify the claim.
entries.note: Marcus reaffirms the founding thesis in his own voice. No deadline is stated.

entries.test: Public evidence of continued substantial human coding through October 2026 would test the prediction that coding would not disappear in the near term after September 2025.
entries.note: “Perhaps” qualifies whether further warnings are necessary, rather than his rejection of coding's imminent disappearance.

entries.test: September 2025 copyright litigation and documented generative AI outputs would establish whether the copyright concerns Marcus and Southen raised remained active.
entries.note: The claim concerns continuing potential violations, not a final judicial determination of infringement.

entries.test: Publicly reproducible examples of generative AI producing outputs closely resembling protected works as of September 2025 would establish whether the derivative-output problem persisted.
entries.note: The normalized proposition omits “as far as I know.” That qualification does not prevent testing the underlying factual claim.

entries.test: The original Twitter replies and public evaluations of their proposed remedies would show whether those remedies could readily eliminate the derivative-output problem.
entries.note: The source rejects the replies they received at the time; the normalization broadens this to claims generally. Persistence alone would not establish that an easy fix was impossible.

entries.test: Public investigations documenting large-scale production and distribution of AI-generated misinformation by September 2025 would settle the claim.
entries.note: The metaphor accompanies a concrete assertion that mass production has arrived.
The source frames exponential growth as a qualified fear, conditional on there being a true exponential. The normalization replaces that framing with an explicit likelihood assertion.

entries.test: Public case records, investigations, and chatbot interaction logs would establish whether chatbots contributed causally to at least two deaths by September 2025.
entries.note: Reports of association alone would not establish the asserted attribution.
The normalization removes “seems.” Neither “so much” nor the relevant set of anticipations supplies a shared test for this broad self-assessment.
The source expresses a collective hope that “we” can learn and find a new path. The normalization narrows the audience to the field and turns that hope into an explicit obligation.
